chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Kirkeby and Charlie Turner keep him out of the Waller band
summary: Kirkeby delayed his return because Autrey knew too much about Fats's money, and bass player Charlie Turner, as contractor, wanted a cut; Autrey says he had warned Fats of being cheated.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: See? Now, we were playing and a certain guy says go out and get me a pint. No! No, I didn't. Some fellow came in and said (and) it was raining like hell in West Virginia, and man, if you've ever been to West Virginia, that's the wrong place to be when the sun is shining, but then when it's raining, Jesus Christ! I mean, you know. said I just heard and I thought [---] So, so this is the way Fats operates on recordings. I said recordings? No, live. I say oh, no. He say oh yes. Like I say. See. I say where is it coming from? Panther Room Bathroom in Chicago. I said what? And he told me what happened. I say -- give him some money. I say go out and get me a pint of liquor. I took the stuff, I didn't -- gullah, gullah, gullah, gullah, gullah, man, I almost went out, because I knew about what was happening. And he told them, he told Kirkaby, call Hermie, get Hermie, I want Hermie.
Now Tom, uh, it's no use you worrying about that now. You -- we can get along. We can -- we don't have to,
because it would do this, and -- he say okay, well you're the manager. You take care of it. He says okay, and he closes up and drink some more whiskey.

So Kirkeby kept me out of the band for how many months? For Quite a while, because of that. And each day I was off, it went farther, and farther, it looked like -- so I was saying to hell with you. I'm happy where I am. You know, and nobody could tell -- it was too damn late. That's one of the things that I held against him. And he did it on purpose, because he wanted me out because I knew too much about Fats's business, and money, and things would happen I had warned Fats. I say man, you being taken! Such and such and such and such. I say we call -- being that -- being a carnival man I saw so much going on.

Oh man, I saw a man with 11 hundred dollar bills. He just sold his cotton. And he stood there trying to win an Indian blanket in the carnival. He lost all that money trying -- he wanted it, and the damned blanket only cost $5.00, four or five dollars. He could have bought one at the store. He wanted to take that blanket home to his family, to his wife, an Indian blanket. He lost eleven one hundred dollar bills. I was on the show. See what I mean?
And I've seen, I know how those things can go, and I saw it happening, and I said well I can't stand by and see it happening to him, when I know what's going on, so I said
they want to get me out of the way. And I say Kirkaby, the bass player, Charlie Turner, yeah, who was a contractor. That's the word I was trying to --

Yeah, yeah. And see Charlie knew what was happening, so Charlie said well cut me in too. Which I don't blame him. You know. What the hell. I knew he was stealing, you look at him, just like a politician. Throw a few bucks my way, and go ahead. What the hell.
And that's what went on. And they kept me -- or tried to keep me as long as -- until he put his foot down, and say I've got to get Hermie. I've got to have Hermie. And matt --
